name: Lienzer Dolomiten
kurzbeschreibung: The striking limestone towers of the Lienzer Dolomiten rise proudly south of Lienz, offering a world-class alpine wonderland for hikers, mountaineers, and climbers.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The Lienzer Dolomiten rise majestically south of the sunny valley basin of Lienz and rank among the most spectacular mountain massifs of the eastern Alps. Geologically part of the Gailtal Alps, their rugged limestone pinnacles and dramatic crags earned them their historic name due to their striking visual resemblance to the South Tyrolean Dolomites. The highest summit is the Große Sandspitze at 2,770 metres, flanked by legendary climbing peaks such as the Laserzwand, Spitzkofel, and Roter Turm. Renowned as the cradle of modern alpine climbing in East Tirol, this range blends pristine high-alpine wilderness, fragrant larch forests, emerald mountain lakes, and welcoming mountain huts that captivate outdoor enthusiasts worldwide.

Route & Anforderungen

The trail network in the Lienzer Dolomiten ranges from scenic family-friendly strolls to demanding vie ferrate and multi-pitch alpine climbs. A premier trailhead is the spectacular Dolomitenhütte, perched dramatically on a sheer cliff at 1,618 metres. From here, a well-marked mountain path ascends in approximately two hours to the Karlsbader Hütte, situated beside the pristine Laserzsee at 2,260 metres. While the main hut routes require moderate endurance and sturdy hiking boots, ascending summits or tackling the famous Laserz via ferrata demands surefootedness, absolute head for heights, and full safety gear including a helmet. Unpredictable alpine weather always necessitates diligent advance preparation.

Besuch & Anreise

Arrival is via Lienz, the regional capital of East Tirol. From the villages of Amlach or Tristach, a paved toll road winds uphill to the spacious car park near Dolomitenhütte. Throughout the summer hiking season, scheduled hiker shuttle buses run directly from Lienz railway station, providing a comfortable and eco-friendly connection. Traditional Alpine Club huts such as Dolomitenhütte and Karlsbader Hütte generally welcome guests from early June through mid-October, serving hearty regional specialties alongside overnight lodging.

Tipps

Do not miss resting on the panoramic sun terrace of Karlsbader Hütte overlooking the crystal-clear waters of Lake Laserzsee and the towering north face of the Laserzwand. Climbers will appreciate the well-protected sport climbing sectors surrounding the refuge. A breathtaking photo opportunity presents itself at Dolomitenhütte at sunrise, when golden light paints the dramatic limestone towers in vibrant shades of amber and rose.
preis: Free access (toll road to Dolomitenhütte charges a fee)
oeffnungszeiten: Accessible year-round; mountain tours recommended June to October
